tasks.notes: Over-broad pin in the M1 census leg: `assert.equal(/(^|[;&(]\s*)trap\s/m.test(code), false, 'the script traps no signal …')` (fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs, section 11) forbids *every* `trap` in fleet/sandbox-boot.sh, where both M1 and the global constraint only require that SIGPIPE is never trapped or ignored. The task itself records that a concurrent run is editing `collect_evidence` in the same script; a perfectly lawful `trap … EXIT` cleanup added there would turn this leg red for a reason unrelated to the claim it grades. Narrowing the assertion to the PIPE/13 signal (the shape the `Check:` command `! grep -nE "trap .*PIPE|set \+o pipefail"` already gates) keeps the leg discriminating without pinning unrelated code. Everything else in this leg is exactly M1: the fixture returns the five BASE lines plus the builtin-guarded sixth and not `json_field`'s line, and the census names nothing in the edited script.; Census blind spot (future-proofing only, not a current failure): `closesEarly` recognises an early-closing `grep` solely by a short-flag cluster — `/^-[A-Za-z]*[qml][A-Za-z]*$/` — so `grep --quiet`, `grep --max-count=1` and `grep --files-with-matches` piped after an unguarded writer would not be named. This is the algorithm M1 prescribes verbatim ("`grep` with a `q`, `m` or `l` in a flag cluster"), and no such long option exists in fleet/sandbox-boot.sh today, so the leg establishes what it claims for this tree; the gap only matters if a later edit reintroduces the bug in long-option form. Adding `|| /^--(quiet|silent|max-count|files-with-matches)(=|$)/.test(w)` to the same `wordsOf(...).some(...)` predicate closes it without touching the fixture's expected six findings.; unverified: the Claim's phrase "every `| head`/`| tail`/`grep -q` reader in `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` either reads its whole input or has its upstream guarded" is established by the census's own algorithm, which reasons over pipeline *segments*: a shell function used as a reader (`| json_field`, `| duplicate_repos`, `| mergeable_field`, `| check_runs_verdict`) is judged by its name, not by what it does with stdin. I read those four at BASE and each consumes to EOF (`grep -o` with no `-q/-m/-l`, `python3 -c` with `json.load(sys.stdin)`), so the claim holds on this tree, but nothing in the diff would catch a future function that closes stdin early and is then fed by a builtin. What would settle it: extending the census to inline (or name-check) the script's own stdin-reading functions, rather than treating an unknown command word as a whole-input reader by default.; Over-strict assertion in leg (a): `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs` asserts `/(^|[;&(]\s*)trap\s/m.test(code) === false` — i.e. that `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` traps NO signal at all. The global constraint only forbids ignoring or trapping SIGPIPE ("SIGPIPE is never ignored or trapped"), and the plan's own Check is the narrower `! grep -nE "trap .*PIPE|set \+o pipefail"`. It holds today (BASE has no `trap` anywhere outside comments — verified), so nothing is unverified, but the second global constraint says a concurrent run is editing `collect_evidence` in the same script; an ordinary `trap cleanup EXIT` added there would fail this exam for a reason the constraint does not forbid. Narrow the pattern to the signal the claim is about, e.g. `/(^|[;&(]\s*)trap\s+[^\n]*\b(PIPE|SIGPIPE|13)\b/m` (keeping the existing `set -euo pipefail` and comment-stripping assertions as they are).; plan-defect: Proof leg (b) fixes the fixture sizes at 80000 lines of `# line <i>` and 16000 lines of `<40-hex>\trefs/tags/other-<i>`, but Machine M2 requires each injected file to be "at least 1 MiB". Those counts produce ~1.03 MB and ~1.01 MB — both short of 1 MiB (1048576 bytes), so the two clauses cannot both be met literally. The submission resolves it in favour of M2: `writeBigFile` keeps emitting lines of the same shape until `text.length >= MIB`, discloses this in its doc comment ("land a few kilobytes short of M2's 1 MiB on their own"), and asserts the realised sizes (`planExtra.length >= MIB && listingExtra.length >= MIB`) after the boot. That is a disclosed, correct divergence and is lawful; recorded only so the operator knows the leg text and the Machine disagree. No edit inside this task's FILES is required.

acceptance.reason: the committed suite is the verification.

deferredVerification.why: Task 1's Context asserts the two unquoted EREs are read identically by bash 3.2 and bash 5 (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, so a macOS 3.2 host is in scope). The sandbox has one bash, and the committed sim runs the script only under it, so the 3.2 half of that equivalence — and the fact that no `shopt compat31` is in play there — is asserted in the plan but not executed by any leg. The bash-5 behaviour, and the agreement with the retired `grep -qE` forms on the refusal inputs, is executed: leg (c) drives `target=smoke` and `run=-7` through the real boot and confirms both still fail before any clone with an empty `git.log`.
